passage:
When the hostel's shared fund came up short, the blame slid toward Aditi. Rohan started it. “She handles the money, doesn't she?” A few people nodded.

Omkar had been about to say nothing. Then Rohan turned to him. “Omkar, you were there, weren't you?” Omkar heard himself say, “Yeah, typical Aditi,” and laughed a little. Everyone else laughed with him.

The relief was instant. He was on the safe side of the room. Aditi picked up her bag and left without a word. Karan, in the corner, kept his eyes on his laptop.

By midnight the warm feeling was gone. Omkar typed a message to Aditi: “I shouldn't have laughed. I know it wasn't fair.” He watched the word “Delivered” sit there.

qa.q: Who did the group blame when the shared fund came up short?
qa.a: The group blamed Aditi, who handles the money.

qa.q: Why did Omkar say “Yeah, typical Aditi” and laugh?
qa.a: Omkar was afraid of becoming the next target, so joining in felt safer than staying quiet.

qa.q: What choice did Omkar make at midnight, and why might it matter?
qa.a: Omkar wrote to Aditi admitting the laugh was unfair, which owns up to the mistake and shows Aditi not everyone agreed.

qa.q: What was it like for Aditi, picking up the bag and leaving without a word?
qa.a: Aditi likely felt hurt and alone, judged by people who were friendly before, and leaving quietly may have been the only way to keep dignity.

grounding: A student joins in blaming a peer to avoid becoming the next target, feels relief at first and then the inner cost.

passage:
“Who left the lab door unlocked?” Tarun asked, arms crossed.

“Yamini, obviously,” said Priya. “She closed up last.”

“I did lock it,” Yamini said. “I checked twice.”

“Sure,” Tarun said. “Jasleen, you were there. Back me up.”

Jasleen looked at the floor. “I mean... she is forgetful sometimes.”

“See?” Tarun said. “Even Jasleen says so.”

“I didn't say it was her,” Jasleen said, quieter. Nobody heard.

Yamini looked at her a long moment. “Right. Fine.” She picked up her bag and left.

Priya laughed. Tarun nodded, satisfied. Jasleen stayed in her chair, her jaw tight, feeling safe and hating it.

qa.q: Who did Priya say had closed up the lab last?
qa.a: Priya said Yamini had closed up last.

qa.q: Why did Jasleen say “she is forgetful sometimes” about Yamini?
qa.a: Jasleen was afraid of being the next target and gave in to Tarun's pressure, even though Jasleen had no proof.

qa.q: What could Jasleen do next after staying in the chair, feeling safe and hating it?
qa.a: Jasleen could find Yamini and admit the remark was unfair, and tell the group there is no evidence about the door.

qa.q: What was Yamini thinking when looking at Jasleen for a long moment?
qa.a: Yamini probably felt betrayed and let down, hoping Jasleen would speak up, and then gave up when nobody did.

grounding: A student under pressure joins in blaming a peer to stay safe, and the relief hides the inner cost.
